name: Oregon
sources: 2026 tax rate charts S and J, standard deduction $2,900 / $5,800 / $4,650, personal exemption credit $260 (none above federal AGI $100,000 single/MFS, $200,000 joint/HoH), federal tax subtraction maximum $8,750: Oregon DOR Publication OR-ESTIMATE 2026 (oregon.gov/dor/forms/FormsPubs/publication-or-estimate_101-026_2026.pdf)

Federal tax subtraction phaseout (federal AGI $125,000-$145,000 single/MFS, $250,000-$290,000 joint/HoH, in 20% steps), MFS maximum at half, 65+ additional standard deduction: 2025 Form OR-40 instructions, Table 4 and line 16 (taxsim.nber.org/historical_state_tax_forms/OR/2025/233803.pdf, Oregon DOR rev. 01-29-26)

Itemized deductions allowed regardless of federal choice; medical over 7.5% of AGI; state and local taxes capped as federally; Oregon income tax excluded: 2025 Schedule OR-A instructions (taxsim.nber.org/historical_state_tax_forms/OR/2025/schedule-or-a-inst_101-007-1_2025.pdf)
provisional: Federal tax subtraction phaseout income ranges are the 2025 figures (statutory, not indexed)
Married filing separately federal tax subtraction maximum $4,375 is inferred as half of the 2026 $8,750, as in 2025 ($4,250 of $8,500)
65+ additional standard deduction $1,000 per person is the 2025 amount for married filers; single and head-of-household filers get $1,200
Property tax cap assumes Oregon follows the 2026 federal SALT cap of $40,400 ($20,200 MFS); the federal reduction above $505,000 income is not applied
notes: Portland-area Metro and Multnomah County income taxes and the statewide transit tax on wages are not included.
Oregon phases out the federal tax subtraction in 20% steps; this estimate phases it out smoothly.
